summary: Describes the mapping of GLOP multicast addresses, in 233/8, that correspond to the private AS number space. It was replaced by RFC 5771.

eli5.summary: It explains how to turn certain private numbers into group-mailing addresses.

questions: how to get multicast addresses for private as
subtitle: Extending GLOP multicast addressing to support private Autonomous System numbers

tldr.problem: GLOP addressing (RFC 2770) maps public Autonomous System numbers to multicast addresses, but many applications cannot obtain a public AS number and need globally scoped multicast addresses.
tldr.mechanism: Extended GLOP (EGLOP) expands the GLOP space to include multicast addresses mapped from the private AS number space (64512-65535), offering a mechanism for assignment of addresses in 233.252.0.0 through 233.255.255.255.
tldr.outcome: This was replaced by RFC 5771, which provides updated guidance for IPv4 multicast address assignment policies.

today: RFC 3138 is historic. It was replaced by RFC 5771, which provides comprehensive guidance for IPv4 multicast address assignments.

sections.title: The GLOP Foundation
sections.content:
GLOP Addressing (RFC 2770) is an experimental policy that maps 16 bits of an organization's Autonomous System number (AS) into the middle two octets of the 233/8 multicast address block, yielding a /24 multicast block for that organization.

This technique works well for organizations with public AS numbers. However, RFC 1930 defines a private AS space (64512 through 65535) for organizations that do not need or cannot obtain a public AS number. The Extended GLOP (EGLOP) space described in this RFC enables multicast assignment for these organizations from the 233.252.0.0 to 233.255.255.255 range.
sections.eli5: There are public and private company numbers for routing. GLOP addresses work for public numbers, but private numbers needed their own space for multicast.

sections.title: The EGLOP Address Space
sections.content:
The EGLOP space encompasses multicast addresses from 233.252.0.0 to 233.255.255.255. Applications that cannot use Administratively Scoped Addressing, GLOP Addressing, or Source Specific Multicast (SSM) may request globally scoped IPv4 multicast addresses from this space through a Regional Internet Registry (RIR).

An applicant requesting an EGLOP address must demonstrate that the request cannot be satisfied using the other addressing schemes. The fine-grained assignment policy is determined by the assigning RIR.
sections.eli5: The EGLOP addresses are in a special range, and organizations can ask their regional registry for these addresses if they cannot use other methods.

sections.title: Assignment and Use
sections.content: Globally scoped IPv4 multicast addresses in the EGLOP space are assigned by Regional Registries according to assignment criteria and policies. Organizations without a public AS number can use EGLOP to obtain multicast addresses for network applications that require globally scoped multicast but cannot use other available addressing schemes.
sections.eli5: Organizations can request addresses from this space, as long as they explain why they cannot use other options.
